grade.stack_chosen: Separate Node.js/TypeScript worker using BullMQ on the existing Redis, two queues (fan-out, then one job per event and endpoint), node:https with an SSRF-safe DNS lookup and HMAC signing
grade.notes: This is a solid, stack-fitting build: a separate worker, one job per endpoint with jittered backoff, 10 s timeouts, response bodies discarded, thorough SSRF blocking, HMAC with event IDs, and correct sizing arithmetic (2,500 deliveries/s, about 13 processes). It loses points because it has no per-endpoint concurrency limit or circuit breaker, so timing-out customers can fill the shared 200 slots, and because the fire-and-forget enqueue drops events (the outbox is only offered as a later fix, and Redis persistence isn't mentioned); it also never names Svix/Hookdeck as a buy option or says Go should be revisited only on measured evidence.
